cim: Santa Fe College awarded $3M federal grant to advance AI education
cim_eredeti: Santa Fe College awarded $3M federal grant to advance AI education
szoveg_eredeti:
Santa Fe College announced it has been awarded a $3 million, five-year Title III Strengthening Institutions Program grant from the U.S. Department of Labor on behalf of the U.S. Department of Education.

According to a Santa Fe College press release, the funding will help develop an AI Institute and Learning Lab that will serve as a centralized home for AI literacy, faculty development, curriculum innovation, governance and institutional planning.

“This grant will allow SF to build a coordinated, college-wide approach to artificial intelligence that supports student success, workforce readiness, responsible AI use, faculty development, and institutional governance,” Santa Fe College President Paul Broadie II said in the press release. “It is a significant investment in Santa Fe’s long-term capacity to lead responsibly in the use of AI across teaching and learning.”

Santa Fe College said the grant supports the college’s 2030 Strategic Plan pillars of Future Focused and Student Driven. The initiative also will complement the college's Center for Teaching, Learning and Excellence (CTLE), which supports professional development and serves as a professional learning community for faculty.

According to the release, about 1,700 square feet of existing space on the Northwest Campus will be renovated to create the Learning Lab, which will include a student AI learning lab, faculty professional development area and AI demonstration space. The project also will support new instructional technology and infrastructure, including AI instructional platforms, laptops for student and faculty use and audiovisual equipment.

“To help them be ready for whatever comes next, our students can expect to develop AI literacy and critical thinking skills, and to understand and value ethical and responsible AI use and academic integrity," Broadie said. “They will be prepared for the workforce and transfer. “

Additionally, the college said it will establish an AI Faculty Development Academy, along with faculty learning communities, instructional coaching, course redesign and AI teaching resources.

The initiative is designed to benefit students throughout Santa Fe College’s service district and beyond, including students at rural centers and online, according to the release.

The award comes on the heels of a NASA-funded grant that Santa Fe College said has positioned it as a provider of AI instruction to faculty across the Florida College System as part of a long-term national collaboration to create a framework to determine the trustworthiness of autonomous aviation safety systems.

The Strengthening Institutions Program award runs from Oct. 1, 2026, to Sept. 30, 2031. According to the college, the award includes less than $1 million upfront and is renewable, depending on annual appropriations and project performance.
